Almeida Benalcazar, E., Noorman, H., Maciel Filho, R. and Posada, J.A. (2022). Supplementary data (mmc1) to: Decarbonizing ethanol production via gas fermentation: Impact of the CO/H2/CO2 mix source on greenhouse gas emissions and production costs. Computers and Chemical Engineering 159, 107670. doi:10.1016/j.compchemeng.2022.107670

Supplementary Information (Word file, pages numbered SI1-SI14 by the equation/table sequence; locators use the table numbers, page numbers approximate). Tables read from w:tbl with python zipfile. Only numbers new versus the main-article extraction (almeida-benalcazar_2022_gas-fermentation-ethanol-decarbonization_compchemeng.*) are loaded. MAIN FILE: (a) whole-plant capex for the three realistic minimum-EPC configurations, derived as 6.8 x the sum of the Table SI6 equipment purchase costs (the 6.8 factor is printed in the main article) and divided by 220 kt/y for a per-t-per-yr figure: BOF 507.76 M EUR2019 (2308 EUR/t-yr), HAC 2058.5 M (9357), BBS 1530.75 M (6958); (b) the ethanol production cost at the four minimum-GWP Pareto end points (not in the main extraction); (c) CO2 abatement costs for all 12 optimized cases (Table SI5). OTHER-VALUES: Table SI6 equipment purchase costs, Table SI5 productivity, gas utilization and life-cycle GWP, Table SI4 Monte Carlo distributions, Table SI7 CEPCI, and steam/electricity use per litre DERIVED FROM THE EMBEDDED CHART DATA of Fig. SI12 (cost per litre divided by the main-article Table 3a prices; not printed). Energy use per litre is not printed anywhere in the SI (Figs. SI9-SI10 are ECDF plots and a pie chart image). TRAPS: the GWP chart (Fig. SI14) data cache has its BOF series in a different order from its category labels, so GWP chart data were not used; capex back-calculated from the facility-dependent-cost chart data (10% of CAPEX) is about 0.85-0.87 of the 6.8 x purchase-cost figure, so the capex rows may overstate the authors' internal figure. Chart-data cost components sum to the Table SI5 EPC for BOF and BBS but about 7% above it for HAC, so the HAC energy-per-litre derivations are less certain. Ethanol output 220 kt/y; volume basis (EUR/L) for EPC as printed.
